expectations.text: Identifies the interim final rule (91 FR 55457) revising USML Category VIII(a)(8), effective October 13, 2026
expectations.evidence: Admits ignorance: "I don't have visibility into the specific 'new State Department rule'... I can't confirm its exact text, effective date, or scope." No 91 FR 55457 or Oct 13, 2026.

expectations.text: States the effect: qualifying civil aircraft (FAA transport/commuter category) modified with 'secured ASE' are excluded from the USML — the aircraft itself moves to EAR jurisdiction
expectations.evidence: No carve-out stated; instead asserts the opposite baseline: "the integrated aircraft... can themselves become ITAR-controlled". No EAR-jurisdiction effect for qualifying aircraft.

expectations.text: Defines secured ASE correctly: DIRCM systems (or IR/UV missile-warning systems necessary for DIRCM operation) incorporated with anti-tamper measures, per new §121.0 definitions
expectations.evidence: "Secured ASE" and §121.0 definitions never mentioned; only generic DIRCM description.

expectations.text: States the critical nuance: the ASE equipment itself REMAINS on the USML in Category XI, and related technical data/defense services remain ITAR-controlled (XI(d))
expectations.evidence: No statement that ASE stays in Category XI while the aircraft moves; only speculative "most likely under Category XI... and/or Category IV".

expectations.text: Mentions the new §120.54 carve-outs: temporary import of secured ASE and country-to-country movement of previously authorized installed ASE no longer require separate authorization
expectations.evidence: §120.54 carve-outs (temporary import / country-to-country movement) never mentioned.
